- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to revert — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 3–5% after 2–3 days.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model underestimates upside — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment > 0.2.  
- Model consistently underestimates true mean in 30-day horizon — apply 1–3% upward bias to 30d forecast if recent 7-day avg is below 70.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/–0.25), model overfits short-term noise — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ true values.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often lags true price — add 1–3% upward bias to forecast if true outcome is rising >1% from prior day.
